claims.statement: The repository exposes script entrypoints for training, real-data preparation, and data benchmarking: `train.py` calls `get_config()` and `train_model`, `data/prepare_data.py` provides a CLI, and `benchmark_data.py` provides a CLI with optional model-forward and JSON output; CI verifies imports of `model`, `dataset`, and `train` and runs the pytest suite.

Real-data preparation is not self-contained in this repository: `data/prepare_data.py` delegates to the external `shared_data.config` and `shared_data.prepare_data` workspace package, and exits with an explicit message when that package is unavailable; this repository vendors the loader under `data/shared_data/` rather than the preparation pipeline.

The preparation bridge converts workspace shards to the runtime cache by sorting manifest entries by numeric index, streaming shard bytes through a sibling temporary file, and atomically installing the destination with `os.replace`; missing or empty manifests fail instead of producing an empty cache.

The vendored loader expects a raw `uint32` cache, memory-maps it read-only, truncates the usable stream to complete `seq_len + 1` chunks, and creates a final-fraction validation split aligned to those chunks.

`dataset.py` is a compatibility shim rather than a second loader implementation: it adds `data/` to the import path and re-exports `PackedDataset`, `ShuffledRangeSampler`, `collate_fn`, `build_training_data`, and `build_synthetic_data` from `shared_data.loader` through `__all__`.

Loader items contain fixed-length next-token pairs, collation stacks `input` and `target`, training order is a reproducible NumPy permutation whose seed is offset by epoch, and validation is ordered; the production loader also configures worker persistence, prefetching, pinning, and training `drop_last` behavior from configuration.

`train.py:train_model` falls back from a missing real-data cache to synthetic data with a warning, while tokenizer-load failures remain soft and use a byte-level tokenizer stub; these paths preserve execution but do not represent a real-text experiment or meaningful generation.

The training runtime owns device setup, optional compilation warmup, BF16 CUDA autocast, non-blocking batch transfer, chunked loss evaluation, gradient accumulation, clipping, AdamW, EMA updates, and warmup-plus-cosine scheduling; exhausted data iterators restart with an epoch-specific sampler permutation.

The model boundary in `model.py` is a decoder-only transformer with a separate input embedding and output projection, pre-norm residual decoder blocks, causal scaled-dot-product GQA, RoPE, and fused SwiGLU; gradient checkpointing is applied per decoder layer during training when enabled.

The training loss path uses `chunked_head_cross_entropy_with_z` to compute the LM head and FP32 CE/z-loss in checkpointed token chunks, so it avoids retaining a full logits tensor; the implementation has an explicit Triton availability error rather than silently falling back when Triton is requested.

Triton implementations are explicit opt-ins: the configuration defaults the three implementation selectors to PyTorch, and `train.py` forces all three back to PyTorch unless `ENABLE_TRITON_KERNELS=1` is present.

Training validation prefers EMA weights and logs loss plus perplexity at the validation interval; generation uses fixed prompts and configured top-k/top-p/temperature sampling and logs a W&B table; scalar training logs include loss, learning rate, gradient norm, timing, throughput, token count, and CUDA memory/utilization when available.

Periodic checkpoints persist model, optimizer, scheduler, step, token count, best validation loss, configuration, CPU/NumPy/Python and optional CUDA RNG state, plus optional EMA state; checkpoint retention removes older step files, asynchronous saves are joined before finalization, and finalization writes separate full-state and weights-only artifacts.
`benchmark_data.py` measures the repository-side synthetic loader and transfer path, with an optional tiny model forward and JSON metrics; its end-to-end and JSON behavior are regression-tested.

The documentation build is a separate generated-artifact path: `scripts/build_docs_html.py` reads a fixed `DOC_FILES` list and writes HTML pages under `docs_html`, while `.gitignore` excludes that output and build tests verify its copied assets and generated portal wiring.

Focused tests define the principal safe-change contracts across configuration, data conversion and mmap loading, model numerics and gradients, synthetic end-to-end training, checkpoint recovery, generated documentation, and documentation-to-code references; CI runs the suite and the reference checker on CPU dependencies.
